name: OWASP Top 10 Prevention
description: Prevents OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities including injection, broken auth, and security misconfigurations.
content:
# OWASP Top 10 Prevention Rules

- A01 Broken Access Control — enforce authorization checks on every endpoint, deny by default, use RBAC or ABAC
- A02 Cryptographic Failures — use TLS 1.3 for data in transit, AES-256 for data at rest, never roll your own crypto
- A03 Injection — use parameterized queries for SQL, escape output for HTML, validate and sanitize all user input
- A04 Insecure Design — perform threat modeling before implementation, apply defense in depth, follow least privilege principle
- A05 Security Misconfiguration — disable debug mode in production, remove default credentials, harden server configs, disable directory listing
- A06 Vulnerable Components — scan dependencies with `npm audit`, Snyk, or Dependabot, update known-vulnerable packages immediately
- A07 Auth Failures — enforce MFA, use strong password policies, implement account lockout, use secure session management
- A08 Data Integrity Failures — verify software updates with signatures, use SRI for CDN resources, validate CI/CD pipeline integrity
- A09 Logging Failures — log all auth events, access control failures, and input validation failures, but never log sensitive data
- A10 SSRF — validate and sanitize all URLs, use allowlists for external service calls, block requests to internal networks
- Apply security headers — `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`
- Conduct regular security reviews — automated SAST/DAST scans in CI plus periodic manual penetration testing
